 On the other side of the door is a world covered in snow.*
*The lights of the town color the pure white snow. On the front door hangs a wreath with a red ribbon and bells, covered in soft white powder. The empty street is covered with a fluffy layer, burying my legs up to the ankles whenever I take a step. A gentle crunch humbly whispers in this tranquil world.*
*The objects falling from the pitch black sky do not look like snowflakes at all. The wind has died down, and they dance around my body. They look more like feathers.*
*It started snowing around noon, and it shows no signs of stopping. The weather forecast said that we'll be getting a record amount of snow this year. Snow isn't anything new around here, but the weatherman smiled and said that the snow makes for a white Christmas. Those words made me realize that today is December 24th.*
*Even with that information, I have nothing special to do as I don't have any plans or arrangements. I tried doing something suitable for the season by playing some Christmas music while practicing my piano, but it didn't cheer me up. I gave up and returned to spending the day like every other holiday, dozing off at a kotatsu.*
*The night wore on while I was dozing off, and it's already almost past midnight. I'm getting really thirsty.*
*There wasn't anything to drink at home, so I decided to walk to a vending machine. It was also a chance to walk in the first snow of the season. I left without an umbrella, and it's snowing harder than I expected, so my body is stained white, as if flour was blown on me. The night air and the snow hit my naked face, making it feel as if I dipped it in ice water. It does feel good since my body is hot from being in the kotatsu, but it's troublesome since I'll have to take a shower when I get home.*
*The road descends gently, and I take care not to slip as I walk.*
*After I finally make it to the vending machine, I brush my clothes off and then shake my head to get the snow out of my hair. I put the handgrip I was holding in my right hand into my pocket and take out my wallet.*
*I can't handle the coins well because of my thick glove, but I can't feel my fingers even when I take the glove off. They must be numb from the cold, which makes things difficult. Giving up, I tilt my wallet instead, and drop the coins into my hand.*
*I push a button and the drink comes down with a heavy sound. I pull the tab open and take a sip. The warmth of sweet hot chocolate pleasantly spreads through my body.*
 I then turn back to the road I came on. I didn't think about it on the way, but I regret that I didn't bring an umbrella, considering the walk home in this snow. I drink half the can on the spot to make it lighter, hold the can with my mouth, and put my glove back on.*
*After I put my glove back on, I drink the rest and throw the can away into the trash can next to the vending machine. I then take my first weary step back towards home when suddenly, I lose sensation in my feet.*
*I thought perhaps I'd stepped into a gutter. I don't feel the usual sensation from my feet, lose my balance, and fall on my hands. My glasses fly off somewhere from the impact. I try to get up, but can't. My hands bounce up and down uselessly on the ground, unable to support my body. I fall on my back into the snow. A thunderous roar shakes the air and pierces my eardrums.*
*At first, I think that a bomb has been dropped. That's how intense the impact is. I can't grab the ground no matter how hard I try, and I can't get up. Bewildered, I think that my limbs have gone crazy. I manage to lift my face and look at the road ahead of me. I doubt what I see.*
*The asphalt is rippling. The buildings are bending like jelly. I finally understand that my body is perfectly normal and that I can't get up because the ground is shaking violently. It wasn't just an initial impact, it's still shaking.*
*The instant I realize that it's an earthquake, my body is flung up into the air and the world disappears again. I hear the vending machine falling behind me.*
*The ground rages like a wild horse. I'm rolling around so much that I can't tell which direction the sky is and which is the ground. I'm bouncing on the asphalt like a roasted bean.*
*I hit my back on something hard, then something soft covers my body. I see white for an instant, but the light is quickly shut out by something. It seems I'm buried in snow. I think for a second that I've been buried alive, but my body is pushed above ground and bouncing on the snow in the next instant. I don't get it. I close my eyes, curl up, and hold onto my head.*
*I hear sounds of trees breaking and things exploding. Large, heavy objects are violently hitting the ground around me.*
*It feels like time is flowing slowly. My head remains calmer than I'd expect in this slow passage of time, and I'm able to think about a lot of things. I already know that this is an earthquake. And its magnitude must be much larger than anything I've ever experienced.*
*I recall a TV program doing an experiment on earthquakes and seeing tables bounce around like living creatures. Would I look like that to an observer standing in a calm place? But being the one experiencing it, I can't tell how much it's shaking. Maybe it's not shaking as hard as I feel it. Maybe I'm imagining things because of the darkness and the snow.*
*But my optimistic thought is quickly rejected.*
*The asphalt is tearing, the buildings are collapsing, and the rubble is dancing on the ground along with the snow. The town is quickly being destroyed. It looks like a dream. This is no ordinary earthquake.*
*The rubble continues its dance. I take part as my body bounces up and down. It feels like I dove into a blender. My limbs may be cut off if I carelessly stretch them out. I don't know how much hope there is in my survival, even if I do everything right.*
*I'm completely helpless against this overwhelming energy. All I can do is curl up, hold my head, and leave everything up to luck. It feels like I've turned into a grain of sand. I forget fear and let nature take its course.*
*I can't tell how long it's been. Common sense tells me it hasn't been long. It felt like I was rolling around for an hour or two, but it should have been five or ten minutes at most. Maybe it was merely two minutes.*
*The time between each tremor gets longer, and the shaking calms down. I sense that the earthquake is settling down. The world eventually regains its silence and the snow leisurely continues to fall, as if nothing has happened. Fortunately, I'm lying on the snow, neither buried nor smashed.*
*My field of vision rises and expands as I cautiously get up. All of the electric lights in the town have gone out at once, and a deep darkness has swallowed the scenery. All that I can see is a field of pure white snow.*
*My body hurts all over from bruises, but it seems I haven't been fatally injured. My clothes are torn and covered in snow and mud, but I should be grateful that this is all that I suffered. I realize there's sand in my nose and mouth, and I throw up on the spot. I vomit the contents of my stomach with surprising ease. Steam rises from the brown vomit, and I can smell the hot chocolate I just drank.*
*I can't find my glasses. I stand there until my eyes get used to the darkness. The world slowly shapes itself as I squint my eyes.*
*The town I can dimly see has completely transformed. Almost none of the buildings retain their original forms. The houses fortunate enough to still be standing have been damaged extensively, but no building is unharmed. The cars have been turned sideways, squashed, or stuck vertically in the snow. I don't see any people, but I hear screams and shouts from all around me.*
*After a while, I start to walk back to my apartment amidst this scenery that looks as if a toy box has been emptied onto it. I must have twisted my right ankle. Here and there the roads are cracked, caved in, and forced up, blocking my path. I hurry on while taking care not to trip over the obstacles. Along the way, I remember my cell phone and take it out, but it's out of service. However, I can still read the time and the display states that it's ten past midnight. It's already December 25th.*
*Intermittent aftershocks rock the ground, and I hear some buildings collapse with each shock. I don't feel anything. Maybe I've had too much mental strain, or something is discharging in my brain. My mind is glowing hot.*
*My apartment has turned into a crooked one-storied building. At first I thought I'd come to the wrong place, but after I recognize the doors and walls, I realize that it's my residence.*
*It used to be a three-story building, but the first and the second floors have been crushed. The distorted third floor is on top of the rubble that used to be the first and second floors.*
*My room was on the third floor, so it managed to stay intact. The door's bent and broken, so I go around to the back to find a broken window. I walk over the rubble, climb past the bent iron fence, and enter my room.*
*The walls are broken, the ceiling has collapsed, the floor is slanted, and steel frames are piercing out from the floorboards. The furniture has fallen down, scattering their contents everywhere. All breakable objects, such as glasses and plates, have shattered and are strewn about the carpet. I see pieces sprinkled in bizarre places, and I imagine what it would have been like if I was in my room. I would have been attacked by the flying pieces, crushed by the furniture, and unable to walk as I currently can. I may have even died here.*
*In the darkness, I watch out for broken pieces as I fumble around to find a flashlight. I manage to find the emergency flashlight, and it turns on even though I haven't used it in a while. The bright light hurts my enlarged pupils, which had grown used to the darkness.*
*I aim the light at the piano, which takes up the most space in my room. The full-sized upright piano had a big ugly top, but a beam had fallen onto it, compressing the piano. The hammers formerly lined up inside the piano are sticking out, and the outside panel has cracked, exposing the wooden cross-section. The wood looks fresh even though it's an old piano. The image resembles organs coming out from a corpse. Indeed, this piano is dead as an instrument. You can't fix something this damaged. Looking at it optimistically, you could say that the piano saved the other furniture from the beam. But there was nothing in this room more valuable than the piano. The realization that the life I used to have has ended finally hits me.*
*After assessing the damage to my room, I start to gather up things so I can seek refuge. Blood begins dripping as I look down, and I finally realize that there's a cut on my forehead. I don't feel any pain even when I touch the wound. I look in some glass and see myself covered in blood and mud, with mangled hair. I want to wash my wound, but unsurprisingly the water's out, so I merely wrap a towel around it. To prevent infection, I wash it with bourbon, which stings my flesh.*
*The cut on my forehead isn't bad, but there may be other injuries on my body that I haven't noticed. It feels weird that I can't trust the sensation of my own body.*
*I don't have a bookbag, so I take the biggest sports bag I have and stuff inside underwear, socks, toiletries, biscuits, chocolates, a radio, a clock, contact lenses, and everything else that may be useful. It's too heavy when I lift it up, so I take some things out. I then change out of my dirty clothing and make sure I have all my valuables. The ground still shakes from time to time and the walls creak ominously, so I move quickly.*
*Lastly, I put on the best coat I have and exit out the window. The wind has picked up and the air sounds like it's weeping.*
*A surreal world sprawls out before me, no matter where I aim the light. There are probably people under each one of these collapsed houses, but my mind doesn't feel anything. My vision is wavering as if I'm drunk on something.*
*The elementary school is the emergency shelter, so I recall where it is and decide to go there. The snow buffets my face, so I raise my hand to block it.*
*It seems like the whole road has turned into an obstacle course. Collapsed buildings block the road, and the pavement isn't doing its job. To make things worse, there's snow on top of it. I can't walk carelessly if I don't want to slip. I have to get on all fours or find handholds at some places. It's a big handicap that one of my legs is hurt and that my right hand has no grip. I fall every time there's an aftershock. Even though it's an aftershock, the tremor is equivalent to a rare earthquake around here.*
*I wasn't allowed to play like this as a kid because I might've gotten injured, but I didn't think I'd experience it as an adult. And what's more, my life is on the line. I'm carrying a heavy load with lots of clothes on, and I'm breathing hard because it's the first time in a while that I'm getting exercise.*
*The transformed town scenery makes me lose confidence in my sense of direction, and the idea that I may be lost makes my heart beat faster. The snow and the wind are blocking my vision and I can't see what's ahead or behind me. I've only walked for a bit, but I'm starting to sweat under my coat. I've heard that it's dangerous to sweat in low temperatures because the sweat will cool down and lower your body temperature. The school's far away, and I don't know how much longer it'll take me at the pace I'm going. I may even get lost.*
*I pass by several buildings on fire. The interiors of the buildings are aflame, lashing out tongues of fire from the windows. Black smoke rises from them, letting out an unpleasant stench. Usually, there's a pajama-clad resident sitting by the burning building, looking up at it absent-mindedly.*
*At another place, a family is huddled up and talking seriously. In one of their arms is a child who isn't moving. At another place, a broken pipe is pouring water out endlessly. At another place, a dog with a cut leash is whining and limping on a crippled leg. I glance at these things as I keep walking.*
*I avoid the mountain of rubble and come out into a road without many buildings. The road is relatively flat here.*
*As I continue walking, I hear a low rumbling sound. Where is it coming from? I can't tell because of all the wind. It seems like it's coming from all directions. Even when I look around, all I see are collapsed houses nearby and white snow in the distance. I don't see anything that could cause the noise. I don't know what's causing it, but I feel something very ominous.*
*Or maybe I'm mishearing an ordinary sound. My ears shouldn't make such a mistake, but I can't say that this situation hasn't taken away my proper judgment. Either way, I can't determine anything right now. I tell myself that it's meaningless to spare it any attention. Giving up on trying to find the cause of the noise, I stare only at my feet, listen only to my breathing, calm my mind, and think only about moving on.*

*It's an old, old, worn-out temple. But it wasn't originally the Daichi Society's temple. The founder... I guess they call the founder Ryugeju-sama, had predicted this disaster and told the people that they'd be safe if they hid in this temple. So several believers hid themselves there.*
*I guess they're living together with victims from around this area. I hear that the temple had been abandoned until then.*
*I can't believe it even when they say prediction. Well, they say catfish go wild and mice run away, so perhaps a person with good instincts could be able to sense the precursor of an earthquake. Or maybe it was just by chance. That's what I thought, but I almost change my mind when we arrive at the temple after having walked through lots of snow.*
*The temple is built on the side of a mountain. Actually, the temple is integrated with the mountain. The buildings are spread out and there are trees and shrubs in the middle of the road, so you can't really tell where the mountain stops and the temple begins. First of all, it's so worn-out that I wouldn't realize it was a temple unless I was told so.*
*Landslides accompany earthquakes. This old temple built on the steep slope looks really dangerous, and it feels like there could be an avalanche any second now.*
Takuma: "How could they think about taking refuge here?"
*Taku-chan sounds stunned. I agree. If I knew that there was going to be an earthquake, I would never want to come near such a place. Even without the earthquake, I'd be too scared to live here.*
*It must be by pure chance the building is still standing safely. Such a thing might happen occasionally, but I don't think it'd be possible to guess that this place would remain standing. And yet, to come here to take shelter in spite of that. I think that if they hadn't known the outcome in advance, it would have been completely unreasonable.*
Shin: "Hmm, maybe there is such a thing as foresight."
*I murmur.*
Takuma: "That's not possible."
*Taku-chan calmly denies me. Maybe he doesn't like these kinds of things. Or perhaps it's because of something Koike-chan told him. Well, I certainly don't think it's possible.*
*The stone steps leading to the temple are clear of snow and in good condition. Believers wearing coats over monk outfits are shovelling. Everyone's lively and working hard. They smile and greet us when they see us. They're all gentle, and express surprise that we survived the earthquake.*
*I explain our situation, then tell them why we came here.*
*We tell them that we're the representatives of the refugees at the middle school, that we want to talk to the representative here, and that we think survivors need to collaborate. Then, we're led to the back.*
*We climb the stairs, and I see an old bell tower along with a bell. It's covered in rust and looks dirty. The clamp it's hanging from has been reinforced with a new one.*
Shin: "Did you guys strike the bell on New Years?"
*I ask the one leading us, and she nods back.*
Female believer: "We pulled out the old bell from storage and hung it up. It has nothing to do with our religion, but we wanted to comfort everybody who survived."
Shin: "I see."
*So they pulled out an old bell that hadn't been used for a long time, huh? No wonder I didn't know about it even though I live here. How old is that thing? Looking at the worn-out engravings on the surface makes me feel somber, but maybe this is the weight of history.*
*There are quite a lot of believers in the temple. There are children, adults, and old people.*
*It's like what we see at our shelter, but what's slightly different is that they're all wearing white, monk's outfits, and they're all hard at work. While I think the people at our place are pretty diligent, the people here are much more so. Everyone's exhaling white breath, moving under the falling snow, and doing some kind of work.*
*They're reinforcing collapsing buildings everywhere, and the sounds of hammers echo through the place. Even the children are walking through the snow and carrying lumber. It's vastly different from our place where the atmosphere's been gloomy recently.*
*We're shown into the main hall in the back. They must have done lots of repairs and cleaning in here. It looks like a proper temple, unimaginable from the outside. But if I look closely at the cleaned walls and pillars, I can still see cracks and other traces of the earthquake.*
*The ones present are me, Taku-chan, and Katou-kun. Katou-kun used to be in the karate club, and he's a big guy. We brought sticks as weapons, but we hid them in the ruins before we reached the temple because it'd be too menacing. We are here to form a friendship, after all.*
*Each of us sits on a cushion, and the three of us are left in the middle of the spacious hall. I don't feel comfortable since the weird statue at the front is looking down at us. I'm gazing about the room when they bring us tea. There are lids on the cups, and there's manjuu to go along with the tea. This is a normal Japanese welcome. It was normal before the earthquake, but I haven't been met with such hospitality in quite a while, now that I think about it.*
*I'm moved as I sip the green tea. It has great flavor. It's food for thought. After a while, a tall, beautiful woman walks up with bare feet. She looks about my age. She bows deeply and courteously, so we bow much more than usual.*
Aya: "Thank you for coming."
*She sits down on the cushion.*
Aya: "Ryugeju-sama is resting right now, so I will listen in her place. I am the manager of this religious organization, Hoshino Aya."
*I falter a bit at the words "religious organization", but I greet her back.*
Shin: "Oh, thank you. You're a beautiful lady. I'm so glad to meet you."
*The lady who introduced herself as Hoshino smiles a bit. Maybe she's not as strict as the words "religious organization" suggests.*
*So, I get to the main topic. I talk about how the public order around here is getting worse, that there's no help from public institutions, how there's less food, and how it's just a bad situation overall. I tell her we should try to get along, and also ask what kind of a place this is. And to finish, I praise her beauty again, and wait for her reply.*
Aya: "We are called the Daichi Society. People who revere Ryugeju-sama are gathered here and are living together. We've stayed around the mountain all this time, so we do not know much about the outside world."

*Taku-chan does have a point.*
*But it's different from the conclusion I came to.*
*First of all, I think groups, religious or not, who live in this harsh environment will come up with their own rules and values. It's rather necessary. We may not notice it, but we may be getting used to strange rules and atmosphere as well. In fact, I think we are. I don't think this is a problem about being religious or not.*
*You can't get along with anyone if you start complaining that another group has a different atmosphere. I don't think you can make friends with anyone unless you open your mind up a bit.*
*I tell him exactly what I'm thinking.*
Takuma: "That's true, but there's a matter of degree."
Shin: "Was there anything really abnormal? I didn't see anything like that."
Takuma: "Well, that's true from what we saw... But you never know what they're really like."
*Taku-chan hesitates.*
Shin: "We'll figure that out little by little, so we only need to adjust then. I'm not saying that we're going to live with them. More importantly, is smoking not allowed here? I want a smoke."

Takuma: "Oh!"

Hibari: "Isn't it amazing? I went to go get dog food today, saw this at the bird's food section, and it hit me. We can solve the food shortage with this. I'm a genius for coming up with this idea from a mere sunflower seed."
Tsukasa: "I see..."
Hibari: What? Do you want to say that I'm speaking on a whim and that I'll have forgotten about it or gotten tired of the idea when the snow melts? Or that I'll be all about something else then?"
Tsukasa: "No..."
Hibari: "And sunflowers are good! Sunflower seeds are seeds, so I'm sure they have lots of nutrition."
Tsukasa: "Um, is everyone going to survive off of sunflower seeds?"
Hibari: "Wouldn't it be cute like squirrels?"
Tsukasa: "...How many would we have to plant if we're to only live off of sunflowers?"
Hibari: "Shut up! Anyway, we'll need to plant a lot of them. And once it's summer, the town's going to be filled with tall, orange flowers. It's like that one song. Sunflowers everywhere, sunflowers everywhere..."
Tsukasa: "Isn't that song about blossoms?"
Hibari: "Is that fact important right now?"
Tsukasa: "No..."
Hibari: "Anyway, you have to help me out too. Here!"
*Kawase-san grabs my hand and hands me the whole bag.*
Tsukasa: "Eh? What can I do to help?"
Hibari: "Hand these seeds out to other people."
Tsukasa: "Can't we just hand them out when we sow the seeds?"
Hibari: "What would we do if I've forgotten about it then?"
Tsukasa: "So you're all ready to forget about it, huh?"
Hibari: "Shut up! You just need to be quiet and do as I say!"
Tsukasa: "I'm troubled."
Hibari: "Here, I'll look after Aroe, so you can rest assured and go."
*She drives me away as if driving away a cat.*
*The heavy bag of sunflower seeds is in my hand now. She says hand them out, but who can I hand them out to, and what can I say when I do? The snow has just started melting, and the people at the school are busy with what's before them right now.*
*I'm at a complete loss, so I walk aimlessly around the school.*
Taeko: "Onii-sama!"
*Taeko calls out to me.*
*She has stopped wearing those ceremonial clothes, and she does her hair normally now. She's fitting in nicely with the scene when she's preparing meals with others.*
Tsukasa: "Have you learned how to cook?"
Taeko: "It's pretty hard. I made light of it. But it's a complex and worthwhile job."
*Taeko diligently talks about her enthusiasm. Her fingers are covered with band-aids, and it shows her extraordinary diligence and also her extraordinary clumsiness.*
Taeko: "It's strange. I thought Aya-san could do anything, but she's not good at cooking. She's worse than me."
*Taeko laughs with that. I try to imagine someone who's worse at cooking than her, but I can't imagine it.*
*The people who were part of the Daichi Society are at this school now. They don't have a good impression of Taeko, and she was the enemy leader for the people at the school, so they hate her even more. I think her position is a difficult one. There actually was a menacing atmosphere, but nothing serious occurred probably because Honda-san took a lot of precautions against it. They're slowly starting to get along now.*
*She may be able to become a normal girl at this rate.*
Taeko: "I'm going to be of use to people even if it takes my entire life. I'll accomplish it no matter what."
*That is, if she can fix her extreme personality.*
*But Taeko looks happy. It must partly be because she can act as a normal person now, but it must mostly be because she's living at a school that she's been so interested in. She looks around the school whenever she has the time, and she comes to report to me about her findings with shining eyes.*
*Every time, I wish I could show her a well-furnished school where students actually attend instead of these wrecked buildings. And if possible, I would like for her to attend school. I'm secretly thinking about letting her go to school once society is restored.*
Taeko: "There are far fewer books at the school library than I thought. It's strange. How did the students attending here play if they didn't read books...?"
*I give her sunflower seeds as she ponders.*
Taeko: "What are these?"
*She tilts her head in wonder, so I tell her Kawase-san's words that she wants to cover the town with sunflowers and that we would be eating sunflower seeds like squirrels.*
Taeko: "Kawase-san's a funny person."
*Taeko smiles, carefully wraps the seeds in a handkerchief, and put it in her pocket.*
Taeko: "I want to see the town filled with sunflowers too. Oh, do you remember our conversation about a book I found at the temple? I researched it after that and found something. It's a really great story. In ancient times, this town actually..."
Aya: "Taeko-chan!"
*Aya-san is standing by the kitchen and glaring at us.*
Taeko: "O-Okay! I'm sorry!"
*Taeko jumps, then runs back to the kitchen.*
*What a busy girl.*
*I then head to the shack at the corner of the school ground.*
*The place is like a prison, and Kuwagata-san's imprisoned there. Since he has kept quiet, nobody forces him to stay here, but he voluntarily wanted this treatment.*
Takuma: "Hey."
*Kuwagata-san's sitting with his legs crossed in the back of the dark room and he cheerfully greets me.*
Takuma: "How's everybody at the school? Are they doing well?"
*I tell him exactly what's going on.*
Takuma: "Oh, that's good. That's how it is, huh? They supported a completely opposite view until recently, but they have new hope now, huh? That's interesting."
*I hear his laughter from underneath the cloth wrapped around his face.*
Takuma: "Well, it has nothing to do with me now. Why don't you leave already? My worthlessness will rub off on you if you stay here."
*He laughs.*
*I speak to him.*
Tsukasa: "Um, you know Koike Nozomi-san, right? Is she doing well with her mother? They seemed to be on difficult terms."
Takuma: "Why are you asking someone who's trapped here?"
*He shakes his head in disbelief.*
Tsukasa: "Well, didn't you get that scarf that's folded up there from Koike-san?"
Takuma: *
"Hah, how were you able to tell?"
Tsukasa: "I just guessed. So, is she all right? I heard that she had a huge fuss with her mother."
Takuma: "No matter what they may say, they have to reconcile. She said such terrible things, but that's how it'll turn out, huh? I don't really understand those things."
*Kuwagata-san hangs his head. I can't see his expression because of the cloth, but I think he's smiling.*
Takuma: "Well, if they can get along, they should."
Tsukasa: "You're right."
Takuma: "But, Tsukasa-kun."
*His eyes are glittering as he stares at me.*

Takuma: "I still don't think I did anything wrong. I'm wrong because I lost. That's all."

Tsukasa: "Oh, yes."

Tsukasa: "These are sunflower seeds."

Tsukasa: "Only if you feel like it. Please plant them if you feel better when the snow melts."
*Kuwagata-san doesn't reply, but stares at the sunflower seeds.*
*I leave Kuwagata-san's place, and realize that I'm walking with light steps. It seems I'm enjoying the task of handing sunflower seeds to everyone. Did Grandfather Cherry Blossom feel this way when he scattered the ashes? I want to give the sunflower seeds to more people, and I remember Yuka.*
*Yuka is sitting alone at the corner of the school compound and looking up at the sky.*
*I sit down next to her on the rubble.*
Tsukasa: "It's a nice day today."
*I say this.*
Yuka: "Yes, it's a nice day."
*Yuka answers in a quiet voice.*
*The sun creates a shadow on her face, and I think her face looks sad.*

*The town has changed a bit. It's still a dreary scene with rocks and concrete lying on top of each other, but the glossy skin of melting snow adds a cute glamour, changing the impression of the scenery.*
*It's a pleasant scene. I create a melody inside my head while I crack open a sunflower seed and eat it. Countryside savouriness fills my mouth.*

Yuka: "The snow's melting."

Tsukasa: "The snow should all go away in about a month."

Tsukasa: "I'd assume they'd rot."

Tsukasa: "I can't tell what's good or bad."

Tsukasa: "Well, if the snow won't melt, we'll just need to think about how to survive on ice. If it melts, we'll have to do something different. Either way, we just need try our hardest."
